questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the climate and the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed the study abroad very much, however the level of education was lower than expected and much lower then CPH.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was a very well organized systems in terms of course catalogue, but assistance with everything else was difficult to get a hold on and contact person didnt take a lot of responsiblity, they sent you to the next office and so on - problem with organisation and help desk in generall.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved a welcome mail and a guide to check in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The check in process was essay, however I was a bit strange to do everything through Zoom.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing I have used a lot of time browsing on Facebook groups, I ended up finding housing through Bologna Univeristys site SAIS, but before I was able to find my apartment I used a lot of time browsing through various sites and writing to many landlords on SAIS, before I finally found an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In my opinion the accomodation in Bologna very expensive, I paid the same price as in Copenhagen which is a way more expensive city in terms of cost of living and at the same time the apartments avaliable for students were very limitied and not in the best condition, I started searching in september for an aparment for the spring semester, which was very necesarry to be able to find a place to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too few options, apartmenets in bad condition and way too expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The webpage was good, however the administrative office was difficult to get in touch with and the fact that they didnt use OLA made the learning agreement a very complicated process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was run through bolognas internal site ALMA RM, where I made a profil and recieved mails with the process from Bologna. I was also at a welcome day with information regarding the courses in end of january, before I started the semester a few weeks later.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was provided with an mail of the exchange cordinator and the university has a site in the internal platfrom where there is Zoom office hours for contacting the exchange student help desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was nicely arranged in terms of the course catalgoue, however I had a lot of challenges beacuse I had to do my Learning agreement over many times, because a few courses weren't avalible in the end, for example one course of 3 Credits said on the site that the language was in English, however it was in Italian and beacuse of this I had to find a lot of other courses to make the "math" go up for the 30 credits.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check up on you new university mail, start early and accept that there are many exchange students in bologna so be patient.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of the university’s strengths is its wide range of exciting elective courses within the broad fields of humanities and communication. The elective courses at the University of Bologna were niche-oriented , offering a diverse array of fascinating and unique subjects. There were many exciting and unconventional electives to choose from, making the selection process both enriching. However, it was challenging to align the ECTS credits because the number of credits assigned to each course varied significantly. This made it difficult to ensure that my overall ECTS points added up correctly.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I have found that the academic standards at the University of Bologna are somewhat lower than I expected. However, the quality of education varies significantly across different subjects. I was surprised to encounter some courses where the academic level and the instructors' proficiency in English were disappointingly low.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at the University of Bologna was more traditional compared to the University of Copenhagen. However, in some aspects, such as preparation and the amount of reading required for each class, it was quite similar to what I experienced at Copenhagen. The biggest difference I noticed was the variation in teaching methods and academic levels across different courses. At Copenhagen, the level of difficulty is more consistent, and the teaching methods within my field are more aligned across different subjects and instructors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Semiotics of Memory 
2. Cultural Mangements of Events. 
3. History of Mass Communication 
4. Italian Pop Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I found the course "Semiotics of Memory" particularly fascinating, especially for those interested in language and modern history. The instructor was highly skilled, and the course offered valuable insights into Italian culture through discussions on cultural heritage.

Another intriguing course was "Italian Pop Culture." The instructor's expertise made it engaging, and topics such as the North-South divide in Italy, along with analyses of Italian culture through film and music, provided a theoretical understanding of Italian culture. These subjects were compelling and enriched my appreciation of the complexities of Italian society.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was not any good options for clubs or sport, but the ESN organisation arranged some sports oppertunites.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were different cultural events avalible such as a talk from Judith Butler, however the spaces was a general problem – they dont have enough tickets for sutdents, chairs a courses, and bathrooms.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend to go to cultural events such as the film festival in june, however I experienced that many of the non academic activites were from the city itself and not the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to resturants, going hiking in some of the parks nearby, going to musueums (most of them are free of charge for students) and going for long walks in the beautiful old streets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Initially, the language barrier posed a significant challenge for me. Navigating daily life, from simple conversations to understanding signs and instructions, was quite demanding. This made the early stages of my time in Italy somewhat overwhelming. However, this challenge also presented an opportunity. I was motivated to learn some Italian, which turned out to be incredibly rewarding. Not only did it help me navigate everyday situations more effectively, but it also enriched my overall experience in Italy. Learning the language allowed me to better understand and appreciate the culture, communicate with locals, and integrate more seamlessly into daily life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As my Italian improved, I found it easier to make friends and and enjoy the local culture. This progress was gratifying and made my time in Italy more enjoyable and fulfilling. Additionally, the effort I put into learning Italian was appreciated by the people I interacted with, fostering a more supportive and inclusive environment - learn a little bit of italian must be my main tip.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Lanaguage barrier as mentioned above.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the Italians' relaxed approach to life and their ability to go out and enjoy themselves instead of staying at home. This cultural trait has been a refreshing change for me. The emphasis on socializing, spending time with friends and family, and savoring the simple pleasures of life, like a leisurely meal or a stroll through the city, has been inspiring. It has taught me the value of balancing work and relaxation, and I have come to appreciate the joy of living in the moment and embracing a more laid-back lifestyle.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start Early in Finding Accommodation: Housing in Bologna can be competitive, so begin your search well in advance. This will give you more options and a better chance of securing a place that suits your needs and budget. Consider reaching out to student housing services, exploring online platforms, and connecting with current students for recommendations.

Learn Some Italian: Even a basic understanding of Italian will greatly enhance your experience. It will help you navigate daily life, communicate with locals, and integrate more fully into the culture. Taking some language classes before you arrive or during your stay can make a significant difference.

Be Prepared for Changes and Flexibility: Academic schedules and course offerings can change, and things may not always go as planned. Embrace this flexibility and be ready to adapt. This mindset will help you make the most of unexpected opportunities and handle any challenges that arise with a positive attitude.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are placed in the correct academic institute that aligns with your study direction at home. This can significantly impact the courses available to you and ensure that they complement your academic goals. Checking this beforehand will help you select relevant and beneficial courses that support your degree requirements.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding aspect was the boost in confidence I gained from adapting and meeting new people and learning new systems, a new language, and studying in a different way, yet I was able to adapt and still achieve both academic and personal goals

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My biggest challenge was feeling lonely at the beginning, not knowing anyone in a new place. It takes courage to meet new people, and it's not always easy, but it's rewarding. Building new relationships takes time and effort, but putting yourself out there gradually pays off in creating meaningful connections.
